Ason Group P0000 - Sydney Industrial Precinct

Executive summary

Meridian Road corridor

SIDRA INTERSECTION 10 modelling results, model P0000m01v15, AM and PM peaks, staged 2028 to 2038.

7

Study intersections modelled (sites 1 to 7), AM and PM, staged 2028 to 2038.

PM peak governs

Every capacity exceedance occurs in the PM peak. The AM peak stays within capacity at all intersections and stages.

pinch points

Without works, sites 1 and 2 (the staggered-T pair) and site 5 exceed capacity (DoS above 1.0) in the PM peak, from 2028 at sites 1 and 2 and 2030 at site 5.

Within capacity to 2038

A targeted works package at the three PM pinch points keeps every intersection at or below DoS 1.0 through to full build-out in 2038.

Assessment

Problem

Cumulative development to 2038 pushes the eastern corridor beyond capacity in the PM peak at three intersections. Site 1 (Meridian Road/Sandstone Road) and site 2 (Meridian Road/Harbour Avenue) first exceed capacity in 2028, and site 5 (Meridian Road/Underpass Road/Beacon Road) in 2030. By 2038 the unmitigated Project Case reaches DoS 1.36 at site 1, 1.36 at site 2 and 1.89 at site 5, with PM control delays of 60.0, 107.1 and 819.8 seconds.

Solution

A targeted minimum works package addresses the three PM pinch points at source: an additional approach lane at site 1 (Meridian Road/Sandstone Road) and site 2 (Meridian Road/Harbour Avenue), and auxiliary turn lanes with channelisation at site 5 (Meridian Road/Underpass Road). A low-cost measure is also applied at site 6 (Meridian Road/Jarrah Street): a turn-lane re-allocation by line-marking that enables a more efficient phasing arrangement. No works at other intersections.

Result

Under the mitigation every intersection stays within capacity (DoS at or below 1.0) at each stage and peak to 2038. Site 1 PM improves from LoS E to LoS B, site 2 from LoS F to LoS B, and site 5 from LoS F* to LoS A*, with PM delay at site 5 falling from 819.8 seconds to under 2 seconds. This supports serving the precinct through staged, targeted upgrades rather than a single large intersection.

Watch item

Site 6 (Meridian Road/Jarrah Street) receives the low-cost line-marking re-allocation and SCATS retiming, but remains LoS D (DoS about 0.9). It is the residual watch item as development proceeds.

Key findings

  • Northern demand dominates. About 57 per cent of development traffic in the AM peak and 53 per cent in the PM peak enters via the northern gateways (Meridian Road West and Sandstone Road). Sandstone Road carries roughly 86 per cent of that northern demand, because the Meridian Road West path requires three right-turns through the staggered-T and the Endeavour Highway is congested.
  • The staggered-T pair (sites 1 and 2) carries the greatest share of new demand and is the governing constraint, reaching DoS about 1.36 in the PM peak by 2038 without works. An additional Meridian Road approach lane at each returns it to within capacity.
  • Connecting the Ironbark Estate North and South precincts internally lets inbound traffic from the north reach the southern precinct via the left-in access and the existing underpass, rather than a right-turn at Jarrah Street (site 7). This eases the southbound right-turn at the Jarrah Street signals.
  • The S14 retail is a major generator (about 23 per cent AM, 28 per cent PM of development traffic) but is local-serving, loading only site 7 rather than the corridor. The warehouse sensitivity confirms the staggered-T is essentially unchanged by the S14 land use, so corridor mitigation is required regardless.
  • A private internal route over the bridge onto Overpass Road could let northbound traffic bypass the staggered-T. The route is on private land and subject to rail operations, so it is a longer-term opportunity to consider.

Land-use sensitivity

S14 land-use sensitivity

Retail vs large-format warehouse

Project Case (no works), 2038 full build-out. Degree of saturation by intersection.

The S14 component (5,260 square metres) is a major trip generator, about 23 per cent of development traffic in the AM peak and 28 per cent in the PM peak. Because the tenancy mix is not yet confirmed, we tested replacing the retail with large-format warehouse. The retail is local-serving and loads site 7 (Beacon Road/Jarrah Street), not the Meridian Road corridor.

Replacing the retail with warehouse markedly unloads site 7 (PM DoS 0.49 to 0.13) but leaves the staggered-T pair to the north essentially unchanged (site 1 PM 1.37 to 1.35, site 2 PM 1.36 to 1.35). The critical corridor constraint does not depend on the S14 land use, so corridor mitigation is required either way. Under mitigation both land uses stay within capacity.

Mitigation upgrade

Targeted eastern-approach capacity

Base (Project Case) vs Mitigation (Project Case + Mitigation).

Works package

Targeted works at the three PM pinch points: an additional approach lane at site 1 (Meridian Road/Sandstone Road) and site 2 (Meridian Road/Harbour Avenue), and auxiliary turn lanes with channelisation at site 5 (Meridian Road/Underpass Road). A low-cost turn-lane re-allocation by line-marking, with SCATS retiming, is also applied at site 6 (Meridian Road/Jarrah Street). No further works at other intersections. Applied from the first stage in the mitigation case.

Works by intersection

Sites 1 and 2 (staggered-T): The staggered-T intersections (sites 1 and 2) on Meridian Road are the main constraint. Each requires an additional lane in both the eastbound and westbound directions to increase throughput at this pinch point. Turn-bay and short-lane extensions are also included: the west-approach right-turn bay is extended from 50 metres to 100 metres, and the north-departure short lane from 140 metres to 340 metres to improve merging.

Site 5 (Underpass Road): Site 5 is the main access to the Ironbark Estate and Kingsford Estate precincts and requires auxiliary turn lanes with channelisation.

Keeps the network within capacity to 2038.
